Title: Finding Frida
Artist: Hilde K. Kjøs (Director & Story Design);Cecilie Levy (Scriptwriter & Original Idea);Bjørn-Morten Nerland (Producer)
Description: In a “real unreality” VR space, a miniature Art Nouveau villa appears before expanding to full scale. Past and present weave together as we step into the world of Frida Hansen — once an internationally acclaimed textile artist, now largely forgotten. Guided by her great-great-granddaughter Cecilie, we explore a lush garden where archival photographs, a gramophone, and woven artworks become portals into Frida’s life. As bankruptcy and profound personal grief descend, the vibrant garden withers into darkness. Four enigmatic female figures emerge, foreshadowing the work Semper Vadentes and the beginning of Frida’s artistic awakening. Across a century, Frida and Cecilie’s lives intertwine. Through art, hardship is transformed into enduring beauty — a testament to how the role models we uncover continue to inspire and shape who we become.

Title: Historically Yours
Description:
Historically Yours is an interactive podcast broadcasting from the Underworld. This work in progress gives visitors a direct line to Cleo, Toinette, and Henri, three fictional hosts loosely inspired by Cleopatra, Queen Marie Antoinette, and astronomer Henrietta Swan Leavitt.

Visitors listen through headphones and send the hosts a question, a grievance, or whatever is keeping them awake. Artificial intelligence transforms each contribution into a new conversation, performed through three synthetic voices. A live transcript accompanies the discussion, while illuminated sculptural heads show who has the microphone.

The hosts are not digital reconstructions of historical people. They are deliberately unreliable approximations assembled from historical fragments, popular myths, and cultural stereotypes. Their appearances, on screen and as 3D-printed sculptures, reflect familiar visual clichés through which historical women are recognised. Their voices are equally speculative: we do not know what these women sounded like, yet synthetic speech gives each host the persuasive impression of an individual personality.

The work draws on the Dialogues of the Dead, a satirical tradition in which historical figures meet in the afterlife to gossip, argue, and judge the living. Here it becomes a feminist podcast in which women who have been celebrated, blamed, romanticised, or overlooked discuss the present from the Underworld. Part podcast, part séance, and part critique of synthetic authority, Historically Yours asks who gets to represent the past and why a convincing face and voice can be so easy to believe.

Title: From Ingrid to Bergen
Description:
Technology is reshaping our relationships and communication with the dead, using the digital traces they leave behind. Decades before these technologies emerged, I was already doing something similar.

From Ingrid to Bergen is an interactive documentary about grief, memory, theatre, and the technologies we use to maintain relationships with what is no longer there. Moving across nineteen years, the project brings together personal archives, photographs, paintings, videos, and texts from different phases of an experience of loss. An idea of a grandmother, a promise, ghosts, forests, neurodivergence, theatre, and Ingrid Bergman form a shifting map through memory and reconstruction, tracing not only the loss of a person but also the loss of what I once imagined becoming.

Title: YOUR UPDATE HAS FAILED
Description:
YOUR UPDATE HAS FAILED is an interactive browser and WebXR experience tracing the digital evolution of SOGICE — sexual orientation and gender identity change efforts. These interventions seek to change or suppress LGBTQIA+ people’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or expression.

A computer anchors the narrative as three composite lives unfold across 1997, 2003, 2016, and 2026, each in a room shaped by its era. SOGICE’s forms evolve: printed questionnaires become software, then wellness platforms, moderation tools, and eventually AI-driven systems that classify and collect data. Blending documented practices with imagined scenes, the work reveals SOGICE not as a single event but as a digital ecosystem spanning “ex-gay” testimonies, promotional videos, exercises, prayers, and data systems. Language shifts toward care and progress, but the pressure to conform remains.

With each update, the system appears new; with each restart, it enters another era; and with every glitch, its limits are exposed. Visitors navigate through a headset, desktop, or phone, clicking, reading, and turning to explore the changing rooms. A dossier accompanies the work, linking sources with the narrative. SOGICE’s apparatus adapts and renews its promise of correction, but its failure endures: queer life persists.

Title: The Grand Hotel Bald Cockatoo
Description: The Grand Hotel Bald Cockatoo is an immersive embodied installation. Based on perhaps the most absurd of Robert Coover’s Grand Hotel sketches, this hotel is a hotel of dreams, in which the hotel manager is a fortunetelling cockatoo. The audience enters a large installation in the form of a bird’s nest. Embedded in the walls of the nest are four large screens, where short fragments of dream narratives recombine. The authors wrote the dream narratives in an adapted exquisite-corpse fashion, using AI text-to-video generation as a prompt. Voice-over narration of selected narratives, tracked separately from the videos, narrates the stories. At the back of the nest, a curtained booth houses a video of the fortune-teller and an interactive fortune-telling device. Guests can press a button to generate a fortune of their own, which is printed for them to take home.

Title: Glass Like Fabric
Description:
Glasslike Fabric is an interactive narrative where the reader scans the world, anything,everywhere, and generates strange stories about things capture by their phone’s camera. Theviewer points at a room, street, object or landscape and presses Scan. The work captures a stillimage, finds shapes within it and outlines selected regions. Red and grey lines, arrows, labels andfragments of equations connect the shapes.

The work uses OpenCV.js to detect edges and colour boundaries, identify contours and selectprominent shapes. Tapping an outlined shape opens a short fictional incident report, assembledfrom prewritten phrases using a far too complex generative story engine. The shape’s typedetermines which opening phrases are available, while its size and complexity also affect thebrief stories.

These are generated stories of places where neighbouring dimensions overlapped, allowingmaterials and objects to intermingle and impact their respective worlds. Trajectories changedirection, glass retains an image, a wall becomes fabric.

With a near infinite number of stories, the work builds new worlds with every new snapshot ofwhat’s around you, ordinary surroundings become imagined incidents, diagrams measure theevidential rate.

Title: Between Page and Screen
Description: An unlikely marriage of print and digital, Between Page and Screen chronicles a love affair between two characters, P and S. The book has no words, only inscrutable black-and-white geometric patterns that, when coupled with a webcam, conjure the written word. Reflected on screen, readers see themselves with an open book in hand as language springs alive and shape-shifts with each turn of the page. The story unfolds through a playful and cryptic exchange of letters as P and S struggle to define their relationship. Rich with innuendo, anagrams, and etymological and sonic affinities between words, Between Page and Screen revels in language and the act of reading.

Title: Bybanen Slop Surfer
Description:
Bybanen Slop Surfer is a playable descent into AI slop: a version of Bergen flattened, exaggerated, and reassembled through the visual language of algorithmically generated culture. The work subjects a recognisable city to the same processes increasingly applied to images, writing, music, and online culture: simplification, repetition, imitation, and endless recombination. 

Bergen becomes simultaneously familiar and synthetic — a cheerful approximation of itself.

Title: Emperor
Description: Emperor, an interactive and narrative experience which invites us to travel inside the brain of a father, suffering from aphasia. Alongside his daughter, we journey into the father’s mental space – imagined as a hand-drawn, monochrome landscape – as she seeks to learn more about his inner self, now obscured by illness.

Title: The Grand Hotel Galactic Center
Description: The VR experience The Grand Hotel Galactic Center is perhaps the grandest of the grand hotels–at a glance–but after several days in the bubble you realize why the rooms come so cheap. The clouds are on an infinite loop. The stars are all flickering. Glitzy exteriors concealing broken-down infrastructure Like a boarding house that is maintained without care. The exotic floor show almost makes up for it. But you sense that it is the same every night, and the performers are just going through the motions. You wish you could see something beyond the banality, but it just isn’t there. You might have loved this when you were a child, but every ounce of your childhood is gone, sapped from you. This is the kind of palliative care you get with the basic insurance. It is a place of wonder and despair. Galactic Center explores text-to-VR environment and gaussian splat as components of a Unity development process. Trigger warning: includes a depiction of suicide.

Title: Her Name Was Gisberta
Description: Her Name Was Gisberta is a VR/2D documentary that portrays the life and death of Gisberta Salce, a Brazilian Trans woman murdered by 14 young men (12 - 16 years old) in the city of Porto (Portugal) in 2006. Uniting the knowledge provided by Virtual Reality Perspective-Taking Tasks, this project was created as a tool of education, social intervention and activism against transphobia.

Title: Goliath
Description: Through mind-bending animation, GOLIATH: PLAYING WITH REALITY explores the limits of reality and a true story of so-called ‘schizophrenia’ and the power of gaming communities. Echo (Tilda Swinton) guides you through the many realities of Goliath, a man who spent years isolated in psychiatric institutions but finds connection in multiplayer games. Combining heartfelt dialogue, mesmerising visuals and symbolic interactions, weave through multiple worlds to uncover Goliath’s poignant story.

Title: The Land of Crystals
Description:
The Land of Crystals creates a moving panorama from archival photographs and historical images of Edvard Munch’s demolished house and studios at Ekely in Oslo. Through the manipulation and sequencing of these still images, the film reconstructs a place that no longer exists, creating a virtual passage through Munch’s working environment and the landscape that surrounded it.

The film’s voice-over is drawn from Munch’s writings in The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, a portfolio of texts and images compiled at Ekely in 1915–16. Several of the archival photographs show Munch in his Winter Studio, creating a direct connection between the written voice heard in the film and the physical spaces in which these texts were conceived.

The Norwegian texts are spoken by an AI-generated voice. This introduces an intentional tension between historical memory and contemporary technology. Munch recorded his voice onto wax cylinders during his lifetime, but none of these recordings have survived, and there is no known surviving recording that allows us to hear what his voice sounded like. The voice in The Land of Crystals is therefore neither an attempt to reproduce Munch’s actual voice nor a historical reconstruction. Instead, it occupies the space between absence and imagination: a technologically generated voice giving sound to words whose author’s own voice has been irretrievably lost.

The title is taken from Munch’s writings, in which he refers to a “Land of Crystals.” For O’Kane, the phrase becomes both a poetic image and a conceptual framework for thinking about memory, geological time, transformation, and the archive. The film considers how technology can reactivate fragments of the past while simultaneously reminding us of what can never be recovered.

Title: The Grand Hotel Sand Fountain
Artist: Scott Rettberg;Caitlin Fisher;Roderick Coover;Julian Pillis;Colin Robinson
Description: The first of the Revisitations: The Grand Hotels of Joseph Cornell series, Sand Fountain is a collaborative AR project by media artists Roderick Coover, Caitlin Fisher and Scott Rettberg that extends one of the imaginary universes of Joseph Cornell's collage series, The Grand Hotels, and the late Robert Coover’s book The Grand Hotels of Joseph Cornell. It takes a kaleidoscopic approach to time, image, language and story through the creation of evocative and entangled narratives interweaving past texts and imagined actions. Three poetic narratives are individually written and collaboratively crafted. The images consist of both deeply personal ephemera and ai-generated images and the narration plays between the human voice and generated speech. The Grand Hotel Sand Fountain is a place of memory and loss. Haunted objects come to life through collaborative methods of exchanging fragments, building fleeting stories, then turning to AI platforms and AR to occupy new narrative environments.

Title: Fiery Sparks of Light
Description:
Fiery Sparks of Light is an AR experience that reimagines a collection of poems by four renowned Canadian women poets - Margaret Atwood, Nicole Brossard, Canisia Lubrin and Sarah Tolmie. It was launched as part of an exclusive hybrid (onsite/digital) programme in Germany that celebrates Canada as the Frankfurt Book Fair Guest of Honor 2021.

Using volumetric cinema technology as the foundation, Fiery Sparks of Light includes an accompanying printed book that contains QR codes that bring  Atwood, Brossard, Lubrin and Tolmie to life as holograms on a mobile device. This enabled Book Fair guests to experience these four poets reading their own original poems, which explore feminist perspectives of patriarchy, gendered objectification, stereotyping and oppression, while further augmented audiovisual after-effects enhance the viewer’s experience. This sensory exploration is designed to elicit an emotional response as users set the stage for these fiery written words to spark to life.

Title: The Fishbowl Leaks
Description:
The Fishbowl Leaks transform(s) the exhibition into a porous virtual aquarium…
Visitors encounter fragments of the surrounding works as marine life and unstable species through a browser-based augmented reality layer. Each encounter alters a personal creature, shaped by the visitor’s movement through the exhibition, transforming it into a generative story.

The aquarium acts as both environment and metaphor. It displays containment but also resembles a collective, developing system. On a shared screen, the aquarium begins in a state of order: partitioned and classified. As visitors contribute their creatures, this order gradually breaks down. Texts detach, species break free, the tank falls apart, and memory is leaking, releasing the creatures into open waters…

The Fishbowl Leaks imagine(s) a living narrative ecosystem. The single artworks start in fixed 
categories and grow together into a symbiotic, participatory collective, by the help of exhibition 
visitors. The result sits between exhibition guide, generative story system, and shared 
hallucination in a container. What might evolve when that container starts to leak?
Themes: Dreams and simulated worlds;Synthetic systems and constructed authority

Title: REALIDAD MITIGADA
Description: Realidad Mitigada (Mitigated Reality) is an AR/Extended Reality App created for the project and hybrid book Realidad Mitigada, a book that collects poems and digital “artefacts” by Tina Escaja (aka Alm@ Pérez). Many of Escaja’s poems and digital works reflects upon issues of social justice, such as domestic violence (Luna Morada/Black Moon) and informatics control (Bar Codes), which makes this book particularly relevant given its potential subversion of traditional technologies that have served to legitimate oppression, such as the printing press. Realidad mitigada / Mitigated Reality is an innovative work created by four professionals in the digital arts. The AR app for the project allows the reader to have an “extended reality” experience that will provide a unique and groundbreaking involvement. The series of stickers located at the end of the book expands the “Virus and the Sea” segment of the book to the community by inviting the reader to place them in random locations, in the way that the QR codes for Escaja’s COVID-19 project have already been posted in cities around the world to collect testimonies about our experiences during the pandemic.
Themes: Language across materials;Embodiment, care, and resistance
